opening: Two UN agencies say hunger will worsen in 16 hotspots over the next six months. The United States disabled another ship running its blockade of Iran, Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye met under their new defence pact, Spain votes on Sunday, and Venezuela plans to lift its ban on opposition candidates.

stories.title: UN food agencies warn that hunger will worsen in 16 hotspots over the next six months, with five countries at risk of famine
stories.region: Global · Africa and the Middle East
stories.body: The Food and Agriculture Organization and the World Food Programme said on Friday that acute hunger will deepen in 16 hotspots between December and May, up from 13 in their June report. Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, northern Nigeria and Yemen face the gravest risk. Conflict drives hunger in 12 of the 16. A strengthening El Niño is behind three of the four new entries: Southern Africa, Central America’s Dry Corridor and northeastern Uganda. Chad was also added, and Lebanon dropped off the list.
stories.whatChanged: The twice-yearly early warning has grown from 13 hotspots to 16, and it ties much of the new risk to the Iran war’s fuel costs and to El Niño.
stories.whyMatters: The five places of highest concern have seen aid fall by roughly three-fifths since 2022, so the agencies’ warning arrives with far less money available to act on it.
stories.uncertainty: These are projections, not counts of deaths or declared famines, and there is no recent assessment for Houthi-held Yemen. The full list of 16 was not in the reporting we read.
stories.watchNext: Whether donors respond before the lean season, and new famine-classification findings for North Darfur and South Kordofan, where the risk is projected to last through January.
keyFacts: 16 hunger hotspots for December to May, up from 13 in June
Highest concern: Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, northern Nigeria and Yemen
Aid to those five fell from $5.1 billion in 2022 to $2 billion in 2025
About 19.5 million people in Sudan, 41 per cent of the population, face crisis-level hunger or worse
67 per cent of Gaza’s population still faces crisis-level hunger or worse

report.heading: What the agencies found
paragraphs: The Hunger Hotspots report, published twice a year through the Global Network Against Food Crises, projects where acute food insecurity is likely to worsen. This edition lists 16 hotspots, Al Jazeera reported, with armed conflict and violence the main driver in 12 of them. Afghanistan, Haiti, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Gaza are rated of very great concern.

Gaza was moved down from the top tier after small gains following the October 2025 ceasefire, but the Associated Press reported that two-thirds of its people still face crisis-level hunger or worse, and the agencies called the improvement fragile. Hunger in the occupied West Bank is expected to worsen.

report.heading: Sudan and Yemen
paragraphs: In Sudan, famine remains a risk in 13 areas of North Darfur and South Kordofan through January. Two displacement camps in South Darfur already exceed the famine threshold for malnutrition, and sorghum and diesel prices have more than doubled in a year, according to the AP’s account of the report.

In Yemen, fighting that resumed in July has displaced more than 300,000 people, mostly around Taiz, Lahj and Aden. In government-held areas, 1.8 million people face emergency levels of hunger, up from 1.6 million.

report.heading: Money, fuel and weather
paragraphs: The agencies point to shipping disruption in the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea and the Black Sea, and to Gulf fertiliser shipments that remain largely halted. Food and nutrition aid to the five highest-concern countries fell by about 62 per cent between 2022 and 2025, and by 79 per cent in Yemen. The World Meteorological Organization expects El Niño to reach exceptional strength. FAO’s deputy director-general, Beth Bechdol, told the AP that predictable funding, and acting before disasters, matter as much as the amount given.

stories.title: The United States disables another ship running its blockade of Iran, as Italy says the drone that killed two of its citizens in Kuwait was made in Iran
stories.region: Middle East · Gulf of Oman and Kuwait
stories.body: US Central Command said its aircraft fired precision munitions into the stern of the Palau-flagged Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman on Thursday, after the ship left Bandar Abbas and tried to break the blockade of Iranian ports. Its crew was unharmed. Italy’s foreign minister said Kuwaiti investigators found that the drone which killed two Italian technicians in Kuwait was made in Iran, though not necessarily launched by Iran. Kuwait summoned Iran’s ambassador on Friday, and Italy is moving its troops out of the country.
stories.whatChanged: The investigation into Thursday’s deaths in Kuwait now points to an Iranian-made drone, Italy is pulling its soldiers out, and the US has stopped its first blockade-runner since early November.
stories.whyMatters: A European government is now publicly tracing a deadly attack to Iranian hardware, while US forces keep firing on merchant ships to enforce the blockade.
stories.uncertainty: Who launched the drone is unresolved: Tajani noted that Iran-backed groups also use Iranian drones, and Tehran denies involvement. Iran’s claims that tankers hit its mines near Hormuz could not be independently verified.
stories.watchNext: Whether a joint Kuwaiti, Italian and Iranian inquiry is formed, where Italy’s troops are redeployed, and whether more ships try to run the blockade.
keyFacts: The Pacific Archer is at least the 15th ship the US has publicly disabled since the blockade began in April
CENTCOM says it has redirected 158 merchant ships
The two Italians killed were Rheinmetall technicians servicing an air-defence radar
Kuwait summoned Iran’s ambassador on Friday, November 27

report.heading: The ship
paragraphs: CENTCOM said the Pacific Archer ignored repeated warnings before an American aircraft disabled its propulsion on Thursday. Ship-tracking data listed its destination as Singapore, Al Jazeera reported, adding that it was the sixth vessel disabled since the blockade resumed in July and the first since November 7.

Iran’s navy commander, Shahram Irani, vowed to break the blockade. The Revolutionary Guards said on Friday that a tanker using what they called an unauthorised route struck naval mines north of Oman’s Al Ghanam Island and caught fire, while a second turned back. CENTCOM separately denied Iranian claims that it had seized two Iranian tankers, that the carrier Abraham Lincoln had been hit, and that it charges ships to cross Hormuz, Gulf News reported.

report.heading: The Kuwait inquiry
paragraphs: The Italian news agency ANSA, as reported by the Arab Times, named the dead as Antonio Saccoccio, 65, and Emanuele Lo Russo, 36, who were maintaining a Skyguard air-defence radar at a Kuwaiti military site. Antonio Tajani said the drone was Iranian-made but stressed that this did not prove it came from Iranian territory or forces.

Iran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, denied that the drone came from Iran and offered a joint commission of inquiry with Kuwait and Italy. Kuwait handed Iran’s ambassador a formal protest over continued attacks. Defence Minister Guido Crosetto told Italy’s parliament that troops based in Kuwait under the US-led coalition would move, partly to Saudi Arabia.

report.heading: Washington’s message
paragraphs: Speaking to troops by phone on Thanksgiving, President Trump said victory in Iran was at hand and that the timing was his decision, according to Gulf News.

stories.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye meet in Islamabad under their new defence pact and condemn Houthi attacks, but announce no military steps
stories.region: Asia · Pakistan; Middle East · Saudi Arabia
stories.body: Foreign and defence ministers and military chiefs from the three countries met in Islamabad on Friday for about two and a half hours, in what Gulf News called the second meeting of the pact’s strategic committee. Pakistan’s foreign minister, Ishaq Dar, said they condemned what he called persistent and heinous Houthi attacks on Saudi civilians and pledged to step up support for the kingdom. No concrete measures were announced, and Türkiye’s foreign minister said no decision had been taken on sending troops into Yemen.
stories.whatChanged: The treaty, signed in Mecca in August, has moved from paper to a working committee that is now openly focused on the Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia.
stories.whyMatters: The pact treats an attack on one member as an attack on all three, joining a nuclear-armed Pakistan and NATO member Türkiye to Saudi security as the Yemen war reaches Saudi cities.
stories.uncertainty: What the members would actually do is unclear: Pakistan has ruled out striking the Houthis inside Yemen, and the meeting set out no timetable or forces.
stories.watchNext: Any follow-up decisions from the pact’s committee, and whether Houthi attacks on Saudi airports and refineries continue.
keyFacts: The Mecca pact was signed on August 7, 2026; an attack on one member counts as an attack on all three
Friday’s Islamabad meeting lasted about two and a half hours
At least 26 people have been killed in suspected Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia since September 23, 23 of them at airports
Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman led his country’s delegation

report.heading: The meeting
paragraphs: Al Jazeera described the session as a meeting of the pact’s strategic political and defence committee, which Dar said reviewed the region’s changing security situation. Pakistan’s army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, attended. Gulf News reported that Saudi Arabia was represented by Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman and Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan, who were also received by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif.
Türkiye’s foreign minister, Hakan Fidan, said no decision had been made on deploying troops in Yemen, and Al Jazeera noted that Pakistan has ruled out attacking the Houthis on Yemeni soil.

report.heading: Why now
paragraphs: Saudi authorities say at least 26 people have been killed in suspected Houthi drone and missile attacks on the kingdom since September 23, most of them at airports. This week a strike on the Jazan refinery killed a Nepali worker, and the Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed 50 targets in Yemen in response.
Gulf News also reported that President Erdoğan had formally signed Türkiye’s ratification of the treaty, following earlier approval by parliament.

report.heading: What it adds up to
paragraphs: The pact gives Saudi Arabia formal commitments from two large militaries, but Friday’s statements stayed political. The three governments condemned the attacks and promised more support without saying what form it would take.

stories.title: Spain votes on Sunday after a campaign that ended with the conservatives narrowly ahead and the far right hoping to nearly double its seats
stories.body: Party leaders held their final rallies on Friday before Sunday’s snap general election. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez told supporters in Madrid he could not imagine losing, and accused Alberto Núñez Feijóo of planning a coalition with the far right. Feijóo closed his campaign in Seville, and Vox’s Santiago Abascal in a Valencia bullring. The last polls, published on Monday, put Feijóo’s People’s Party narrowly ahead; most suggested it could govern with Vox, though some had the two short of a majority. About 38.6 million people can vote.
stories.whatChanged: The campaign is over and Saturday is a legally required day of reflection, with no new polls allowed since Monday.
stories.whyMatters: A People’s Party government relying on Vox would give a far-right party a share of national power for the first time since Franco’s death, after an election fought largely over housing.
stories.uncertainty: Polls disagreed: the state-run CIS institute had Sánchez’s Socialists first, while most private pollsters had the People’s Party ahead. A hung parliament and even a repeat election are possible.
stories.watchNext: Turnout figures at 2:30 PM and 6:30 PM local time on Sunday and the first results from 9 PM, then whether any bloc reaches 176 of 350 seats.
keyFacts: 350 seats in Congress; 176 are needed for a majority
38,616,949 people are eligible to vote, including 2.66 million abroad
In 2023 the People’s Party won 137 seats, and with Vox held 170
Postal votes accepted: 1,012,033, well below 2023’s 2.47 million
Polling stations open from 9 AM to 8 PM; Congress first sits on December 23

report.heading: The final day
paragraphs: Sánchez closed his campaign at Madrid’s Caja Mágica arena, which his party said drew 13,000 people, setting a target of 75 per cent turnout and a progressive majority. Feijóo, after a stop in Barcelona, promised decency and good government in Seville and repeated a pledge to build a million homes in four years. Abascal, whose party hopes to almost double the 33 seats it won in 2023, campaigned on what Vox calls national priority and remigration, the BBC reported.

Ada Colau, Irene Montero and Yolanda Díaz held separate rallies for the left. Feijóo said his party had never discussed giving Vox ministerial posts, though the People’s Party already governs with Vox in several regions.

report.heading: Late controversies
paragraphs: Feijóo faced renewed questions about photographs, published in 2013, showing him in the 1990s with a convicted drug trafficker, and was challenged over a debate claim about pensions, Gulf Times reported. On Friday the People’s Party complained to the Central Electoral Board about postal-vote papers found in a Madrid container, El Constitucional reported, while Abascal warned of possible tricks without offering evidence.

report.heading: What happens next
paragraphs: If no candidate wins an absolute majority in a first investiture vote, a simple majority suffices 48 hours later. If nobody wins a confidence vote within two months, parliament is dissolved, as happened before the repeat elections of 2016 and 2019, idealista noted. The official count begins on Friday, December 4.

stories.title: Venezuela’s interim authorities say they will repeal the 2024 law used to bar opposition figures from public office
stories.body: National Assembly president Jorge Rodríguez announced on Thursday that the law will be scrapped. Passed in 2024, after the disputed election that kept Nicolás Maduro in power, it targeted people accused of promoting sanctions against Venezuela and was criticised as a tool of persecution. Rodríguez said it belonged to a very specific moment and that the transition talks with the opposition had agreed to review several laws. The same day, opposition leader María Corina Machado began a campaign of neighbourhood assemblies across the country.
stories.whatChanged: Days after a fourth round of talks ended without an election date, the government has offered its first concrete legal concession to the opposition.
stories.whyMatters: The law was one of the tools used to keep opponents off the ballot, so repealing it is a precondition for the competitive election the interim government has promised but not scheduled.
stories.uncertainty: No repeal text or vote date has been published, and it is not yet clear whether earlier disqualifications, including Machado’s, will be lifted. This account rests on one wire-based report.
stories.watchNext: A National Assembly vote on the repeal, and whether the talks produce an election date or a new electoral council.
keyFacts: Announced by National Assembly president Jorge Rodríguez on November 26
The law was passed in 2024 and targeted people who promoted or supported sanctions
Delcy Rodríguez has led an interim government since US forces seized Maduro in January
Machado’s team said about 2,000 neighbourhood assemblies met on the first day

report.heading: The announcement
paragraphs: Jorge Rodríguez, who leads the National Assembly and is the brother of interim leader Delcy Rodríguez, said the law had responded to particular circumstances and would be repealed, Al Jazeera reported, citing AFP. He said the dialogue with opposition figures chosen with Washington’s involvement had agreed to review a number of laws.

report.heading: Background
paragraphs: The law was approved after the 2024 vote that Maduro claimed amid allegations of fraud, and critics said its penalties for anyone who backed sanctions made it a tool for punishing dissent. Delcy Rodríguez has governed since US forces seized Maduro in January. At the United Nations in September she promised free elections but gave no date. The fourth round of transition talks ended this week without an election date or agreement on a new electoral council.
Machado, who was legally barred from running in 2024, returned from exile last month and is widely expected to stand if an election is called.

report.heading: The opposition’s next move
paragraphs: On Thursday Machado launched neighbourhood assemblies built around 19 questions. Her team told AFP that about 2,000 meetings took place on the first day and that it expects more than a million people to take part over several months. The effort looks designed to build an organisation ready for a vote whenever one is called.

stories.title: Ukraine says a counteroffensive in northern Kharkiv has retaken about 200 square kilometres and 14 settlements
stories.whatChanged: Ukraine’s command gave the first figures for Operation Bear Trap, which it says is still going on.
stories.body: Ukraine’s military says the operation, which became public on November 20, used deception, rear attacks and drone-laid mines on supply routes to stop a Russian push for almost 500 square kilometres. Russia still holds at least four border villages in the area, including Vovchansk, Al Jazeera reported. The claims have not been independently confirmed. The report also noted that US-brokered proposals on security guarantees remain under discussion, with President Zelensky saying he does not trust a deal struck between Washington and Moscow.

stories.title: Guinea-Bissau’s military rulers postpone elections by two years, to November 2028
stories.whatChanged: Presidential and legislative elections due on December 6 were pushed back on the first anniversary of last year’s coup.
stories.body: A decree from the transitional president, Major General Horta Inta-a, cited insufficient technical, material and financial conditions. The army seized power in November 2025, interrupting a presidential vote and ousting Umaro Sissoco Embaló, and was meant to oversee a one-year transition. The West African bloc ECOWAS has called for a short, structured return to civilian rule.

stories.body: Niger’s defence ministry said heavily armed attackers struck the compound at Sanam, in the Tillabéri region near Mali, early on Thursday, killing at least 13 and wounding 20, a toll it called provisional. No group has been named. Two days earlier the ministry blamed Boko Haram for an attack in Diffa that killed 11 soldiers.

stories.body: Costa Rica’s immigration chief said she was the subject of an international alert over links to terrorist acts, without saying which country issued it. stories.body: The Drug Enforcement Administration launched the line this week, inviting tips by Signal, WhatsApp and email on suspected traffickers and corrupt officials, with a focus on Sinaloa. stories.title: Restricted Nvidia Blackwell hardware is traced to a Shanghai data-centre site linked to Alice Huang, days before Jensen Huang faces Congress
stories.body: Bloomberg reported on Friday that loan filings to Chinese regulators show Nvidia’s most advanced systems at a Shanghai site called the Yangtze River Delta Project. One company, Shanghai Shuoyao, pledged a GB300 NVL72 rack, which holds 72 Blackwell Ultra chips, as collateral for a 96 million yuan loan, about $14 million. Another, Shanghai Kezhan, listed a GB200 server. Shipping such chips to China requires a US licence. Bloomberg traced the rack’s serial number to Taiwan’s Gigabyte, which would not say who bought it.
stories.whatChanged: For the first time, documents place Blackwell-generation hardware inside China, at a site with ties to the woman at the centre of Nvidia’s leadership crisis.
stories.whyMatters: It is concrete evidence that the most restricted US AI chips can still reach China, arriving just before lawmakers question Nvidia about its controls.
stories.hook: A paper trail, not a smuggling verdict: the filings show where the hardware ended up, not how it got there.
stories.uncertainty: Bloomberg says it has no evidence that Megaspeed, the Singapore broker Alice Huang founded, sent the hardware, and Megaspeed denies wrongdoing. The filings cover only equipment pledged for loans, so the site’s full contents are unknown.
stories.watchNext: Jensen Huang’s closed-door interview with House committees on December 1 and the public Senate Banking Committee hearing on export controls on December 3.
keyFacts: A GB300 NVL72 rack with 72 Blackwell Ultra chips was pledged for a 96 million yuan loan from Shanghai Innovation Bank
Shanghai Kezhan also listed a GB200 server and 32 servers with H200 chips
Local media say the site is designed for up to 800,000 servers
The US blacklisted Megaspeed this month; the Justice Department is investigating it

report.heading: What the filings show
paragraphs: According to Bloomberg’s reporting, as relayed by The Next Web, Engadget and IBTimes, Shuoyao’s loan came from Shanghai Innovation Bank, while Kezhan described its GB200 server when it took a 90 million yuan loan in late 2025 from a leasing firm owned by a Shanghai government agency. A sister company of Shuoyao disclosed Hopper-generation servers made by Super Micro and Dell; it is unclear whether those had US approval.
Gigabyte said it follows applicable laws and its own compliance rules, but declined to name the rack’s first buyer.

report.heading: The Alice Huang link
paragraphs: Shuoyao says it is one of Megaspeed’s service providers but calls the relationship ordinary commercial cooperation. Megaspeed used a rendering of the Shanghai project in a 2024 investor pitch without naming the country, Bloomberg found. Engadget reported that Kang Wei, whom The New York Times has described as often introduced as Alice Huang’s husband, is listed as the facility’s president.
Neither Nvidia nor Megaspeed answered Bloomberg’s questions. The reporting follows Nvidia’s reinstatement of Jensen Huang as chief executive on November 23.

report.heading: Why Washington cares
paragraphs: President Trump has said he does not want Blackwell chips going to China, and shipping them there requires a US licence. Lawmakers are expected to press Huang on how far Nvidia can see where its chips end up once they pass through resellers and server makers.

stories.title: The first generic doses of a twice-yearly HIV prevention injection arrive in Africa, starting with Zambia
stories.body: The Global Fund said on Wednesday that the world’s first deliveries of generic lenacapavir have reached Zambia, with Uganda expecting supplies within days and Zimbabwe early next year. The injection, given every six months, protects people who do not have HIV from infection. The deliveries come a year after Gilead’s branded version reached sub-Saharan Africa. More than 189,000 people in 10 early-adopter countries have had a first dose, and the Fund and the US government aim to reach at least three million people by the end of 2028.
stories.whatChanged: Lenacapavir has moved from the originator company’s supply to cheaper generic production, which is what large-scale rollout depends on.
stories.whyMatters: An injection that lasts six months offers an alternative to daily pills, and generic supply is what allows the volumes the Global Fund is planning.
stories.hook: A supply milestone rather than a new medical result: the drug’s effect is established, and the test now is how many people it reaches.
stories.uncertainty: The Global Fund did not name the generic manufacturers or say what the generic doses cost. Uganda’s delivery was expected, not confirmed, at the time of the announcement.
stories.watchNext: Larger generic shipments to many more countries in the first quarter of 2027, and whether 24 countries have the drug by the end of this year as planned.
keyFacts: First generic deliveries arrived in Zambia, announced on November 25, 2026
More than 189,000 people in 10 countries have received a first dose
24 countries are expected to have lenacapavir by the end of 2026
The 2027 delivery volume is planned at four times 2026’s

report.heading: What arrived
paragraphs: The Global Fund announced the Zambian delivery from Geneva and said a shipment to Uganda would follow in the coming days, with one it is financing due in Zimbabwe in early 2027. A digest of African reporting by allAfrica on Friday likewise described Uganda as about to receive its first generic supplies.

The Fund credited Gilead’s early voluntary licences with generic makers, investment by the Gates Foundation and Unitaid, and technical support funded with the Children’s Investment Fund Foundation. It said its expert review process and a recent US Food and Drug Administration approval had allowed faster purchasing through its pooled platform.

report.heading: The scale of the plan
paragraphs: Together with the US government, the Global Fund plans to deliver four times this year’s volume in 2027 and to reach at least three million people by the end of 2028. Gilead’s own product will keep flowing during the switch to generics. The Fund describes the injection as nearly 100 per cent effective at preventing infection, a figure drawn from earlier clinical trials rather than from this rollout.
Its executive director, Peter Sands, called the arrival of generics a major breakthrough, while its head of supply operations said more quality-assured suppliers are still needed.

report.heading: The limits
paragraphs: The release gives no generic price and does not name the manufacturers, so the savings cannot yet be judged. Reaching people also depends on clinics, testing and follow-up visits every six months.

briefs.title: Argentina bars its central bank from printing money to fund the government
briefs.text: Argentina’s Chamber of Deputies gave final approval on Thursday, by 141 votes to none with 99 abstentions, to a law making the preservation of the currency’s value the central bank’s main mission and ending money-printing to cover public spending. The Senate had removed President Javier Milei’s proposal to require two-thirds majorities to dismiss the bank’s governors. Separately, the Senate voted 43 to 29 to suspend the primaries before the 2027 presidential race; that bill now goes to the lower house.

europe.summary: Spain ends its campaign before Sunday’s vote, Italy moves its troops out of Kuwait after two citizens were killed, and Ukraine reports gains in northern Kharkiv and new strikes inside Russia.

briefs.title: Ukraine says it hit a Russian plant that makes an ingredient for missile fuel
briefs.text: Ukraine’s General Staff said forces struck the Efremov synthetic rubber plant in Russia’s Tula region overnight on Friday, working with a resistance group; the plant’s product is used in solid fuel for Iskander missiles, and damage was still being assessed. The military also said an earlier strike on the Novoshakhtinsk refinery in Rostov destroyed 20 storage tanks.

briefs.title: Nine more Ukrainian children are returned through Melania Trump’s mediation
briefs.text: President Zelensky said on Friday that nine children, the youngest aged eight, had been brought back from Crimea and occupied parts of the Zaporizhzhia and Kherson regions with the help of the US first lady. He put the total number of children returned to Ukraine at 2,875, without giving a timeframe.

africa.summary: UN agencies put Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia and northern Nigeria among the places at highest risk of famine, Guinea-Bissau’s junta delays elections to 2028, and the first generic HIV prevention injections reach Zambia.

briefs.title: Zambia bans a protest against removing presidential term limits
briefs.text: Police in Zambia banned a march planned for November 25 against a petition to scrap presidential term limits, citing the risk of clashes with a rival pro-government rally. Three groups aligned with the governing party have asked parliament to remove the limits, which would let President Hakainde Hichilema stay beyond 2031; ministers say he is not seeking a third term, and the organisers have appealed.

middle-east.summary: The US disables another ship running its Iran blockade, Italy says the drone that killed two Italians in Kuwait was Iranian-made, and Saudi Arabia’s pact partners condemn Houthi attacks.

briefs.title: Eisenkot says he will try to form an Israeli government in the time left on his mandate
briefs.text: Gadi Eisenkot, the opposition leader tasked with forming a government, said he intends to do so within the eight days remaining and accused Likud of stalling unity talks, Gulf News reported, citing Xinhua; Likud called it a double game. Al Jazeera’s analysis notes that his bloc cannot win a confidence vote alone and that a rotation deal with Netanyahu would break his campaign promise.

asia.summary: Pakistan hosts the Mecca defence pact’s ministers, and loan filings place restricted Nvidia hardware at a Shanghai data-centre site.

oceania.summary: Australia sanctions two men it accuses of acting for Iran’s Revolutionary Guards, as New Zealand’s parties keep negotiating after the final count.

briefs.title: Australia sanctions two alleged agents of Iran over antisemitic arson attacks
briefs.text: Australia imposed sanctions on Zohair Hassib and Kazem Hamad, whom it accuses of acting as proxies for Iran’s Revolutionary Guards in arson attacks on Jewish targets in Sydney and Melbourne in 2024, Gulf News and Khaleej Times reported on Friday.
